payload.purpose_context: Several Spec Kitty commands write to disk in ways that can silently harm a user: spec-kitty init can truncate an unrelated file a local attacker points at via a predictable shared-temp lock; concurrent mission activity can drop decision records so the index disagrees with the event log; and re-running init can delete a user's custom missions and memory notes. This mission closes those defect classes so routine commands are trustworthy on shared machines and under concurrency.
payload.purpose_tldr: Make Spec Kitty's on-disk writes safe: no symlink-hijack file truncation, no lost concurrent decision records, and no destruction of user-authored project content.

payload.question: When spec-kitty init finds user-authored .kittify/missions or memory but no config.yaml, what should it do?

payload.final_answer: Back up, then proceed: when init re-runs on a populated .kittify/ that is missing config.yaml, move existing operator-authored content (custom missions, memory notes) into a timestamped .kittify/.backup-<UTC-timestamp>/ before copying scaffold, and report the backup path to the user. Never rmtree operator-owned content.
